title: Pointer Creation vs Dereference
goal: Convert a reference to a raw pointer and dereference it inside an unsafe block.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Raw Pointers

hints: Casting a reference to a raw pointer is safe and uses standard casting syntax.
Reading memory behind a raw pointer requires dereferencing it inside an unsafe block.
explanation: Converting a mutable reference `val` to a raw pointer `*mut i32` is safe Rust using `val as *mut i32`. Casting `val` directly to an integer or dereferencing `*val` first produces type conversion errors (`E0605`). Reading the value behind `ptr` requires dereferencing `*ptr` inside an `unsafe` block (`unsafe { *ptr }`). Doing `*ptr` outside `unsafe` triggers `E0133`, while returning `ptr` directly yields a raw pointer instead of `i32` (`E0308`).
